title: Tenant shaping and dynamic burst fabric PRD notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic design proposal (PRD-like notes) for a Tenant Shaping + Dynamic Burst Fabric feature set for Dedicated capacity. Goal is to provide predictable isolation for committed usage while allowing safe, cost-aware bursts and graceful reclaim during contention.

Scope and motivation:
- Customers on Dedicated want strong throughput guarantees for baseline workloads (reserved capacity) but also the ability to burst for short events without long procurement cycles.
- Existing reserved pools are too binary: either fully reserved (underutilized) or hard-throttled when saturated.
- We need a middle ground that lets tenants consume extra ephemeral capacity with controllable economic and latency tradeoffs while protecting critical SLAs.

Primary objectives:
1) Provide per-tenant shaping that enforces baseline throughput + latency SLOs for committed capacity.
2) Offer a dynamic burst fabric that grants short-term excess tokens to tenants when capacity is idle or via pre-specified credit purchases.
3) Ensure graceful, predictable reclaim behavior under contention with transparent signals to customers.
4) Keep operating complexity low and provide operators clear telemetry for debugging fairness/cost disputes.

High-level concepts:
- Baseline Reservation: tenant reserves N slots / vGPU-equivalent units that map to steady throughput. These are protected by a hard SLO and give priority in scheduling.
- Shaping Token Bucket: each tenant has a steady-state token bucket rate derived from their reservation. Tokens correspond to scheduling credits (e.g., model-invocation units or vGPU-ms).
- Burst Fabric: a shared pool of ephemeral credits (soft capacity) that can be granted to tenants on demand. Grants are time-limited and tagged with a reclaim policy.
- Credit Types:
  * SoftBurstCredit: free/borrowed from idle capacity. Lower priority, preemptible.
  * PaidBurstCredit: purchased burst credits (pre-committed monthly or on-demand), higher retention before reclaim and billing at premium rate.
  * PrewarmReservation: ephemeral prewarmed slots for cold-start sensitive customers; higher cost but faster tail latency.
- Isolation modes: soft (best-effort burst), mixed (partitioned burst pool per tenant group), strict (no burst, reserved-only).

APIs and config (proposal):
- TenantConfig {
  reserved_units: 8,
  shaping_window_s: 60,
  max_burst_ratio: 4.0, // up to 4x throughput for short windows
  burst_mode: "auto|paid|disabled",
  preferred_reclaim: "latency|cost|fairness"
}
- Admin endpoints: purchase_burst_credits(tenant_id, units, duration), set_isolation_mode(tenant_group, mode)
- Runtime signals: X-Burst-Grant: {type, units, expires_at, reclaim_priority}

Burst grant lifecycle:
1) Request arrives; scheduler checks tenant token bucket and reserved slots.
2) If insufficient tokens, scheduler attempts to grant from burst fabric according to policy and tenant eligibility.
3) When idle capacity exists, automated background grants top-up low-credit tenants up to max_burst_ratio.
4) Grants are issued with an expiry and reclaim priority.
5) Under contention grants are reclaimed using reclaim policies (preempt oldest/lowest-priority grant first, or cheapest/lowest-latency-sensitive tenants first).

Reclaim policies and customer experience:
- Customers receive explicit HTTP headers or events when a grant is reduced or reclaimed: X-Burst-Reclaim-Notice with short TTL (e.g., 8–30s) to allow callers to fallback to smaller prompts or degrade noncritical features.
- PaidBurstCredit grants have higher grace (e.g., 60–120s) before reclaim.
- Metrics surfaced to customers: current_reserved_usage, burst_in_use, recent_reclaims, reclaim_count_by_window.

Scheduling & fairness model:
- Weighted fair queuing across tenants' reserved units. Burst fabric gets a lower scheduling priority but may be allocated aggressively when overall utilization < target (e.g., 75%).
- When utilization > threshold, enforce fairness by proportional reduction capped by per-tenant min-reservation.
- Maintain per-tenant moving-average fairness score; use it to deprioritize abusers when granting ephemeral bursts.

Operational telemetry and alerts:
- Key metrics to emit: reserved_p95_latency, burst_p95_latency, burst_grants_per_minute, burst_reclaims_per_minute, burst_pool_utilization, fairness_index, disputed_billing_events.
- Alerts: sustained burst_reclaims_rate > 5/min for 5m, burst_pool_utilization > 95% for 3m, fairness_index drop > 20% in 15m.

Costing and billing model:
- Free soft bursts when idle (no bill), but reclaimed quickly.
- PaidBurstCredits: pre-purchased monthly packs or on-demand at premium per-unit-minute.
- Billing line items: reserved_capacity_charge, paid_burst_charge, prewarm_fee. Provide daily usage reports and per-tenant cost breakdown in Console.

Runbook snippets (operator-facing):
- High burst reclaim rate investigation: check recent scheduling logs -> look for tenants with abnormally high bursts consumed -> examine fairness scores and purchase history -> contact CS if paid_burst disputes.
- Emergency drain: set isolation_mode=strict for affected pool; notify customers via status page; escalate to SRE.

Implementation phasing (minimal viable to full):
MVP (Q1):
- Implement shaping token bucket for reserved units.
- Simple global burst_pool (soft bursts) with automatic topups when utilization < 70%.
- Emit headers/events for grant/reclaim. Billing: none (soft-only).

Phase 2 (Q2):
- PaidBurstCredits purchase flow + billing integration.
- Per-tenant fairness scoring + proportional reclaim.
- Console surfaces: burst usage and reclaim events.

Phase 3 (Q3):
- Partitioned burst pools, prewarm reservations, advanced reclaim heuristics (latency-first, cost-first).
- Admin APIs for bulk purchases and tenant groups.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to map tokens to real infra units (model size matters). Proposal: normalize credits to normalized-vGPU-ms per model-family with conversion table maintained by model catalog.
- Can we make grants transferable across regions? Complexity vs benefit.
- Risk: noisy-tenant attack where many tenants consume bursts aggressively; mitigations: cap burst_rate_per_tenant, require paid purchase for sustained high burst.
- Accounting latency: billing must reconcile reclaimed minutes precisely; design needs fine-grained accounting hooks in scheduler.

Customer-facing UX examples:
- Console: slider to set max_burst_ratio and burst_mode. Billing preview shows incremental cost for paid bursts.
- API example: when application receives X-Burst-Reclaim-Notice, it should: retry with smaller prompt, or call fallback model, or queue the request.

Acceptance criteria (for launch):
- Baseline reserved p95 latency unchanged within 5% compared to pre-feature baseline under mixed load tests.
- Burst grants reduce 95th percentile cold failure rate for eligible tenants by > 40% during traffic spikes in synthetic tests.
- Billing for paid bursts reconciles to < 2% discrepancy over a 24h window.
- SRE runbook validated by a simulated runaway tenant test.

Notes / related work:
- Align with Dedicated capacity tenancy isolation workstream and autoscaler team (see linked artifacts).
- This proposal intentionally separates the "shaping" control plane (per-tenant tokens + policies) from the serving runtime scheduler; runtime only enforces tokens and grants.

Next actions (owners):
- Prod: define metric specs and dashboards (Marcus).
- Billing: define metering vs billing events for paid burst (Aditi).
- Eng: prototype token bucket enforcement and grant headers in a canary pool (Jonas).
- PM: customer interview with three Dedicated customers to validate burst expectations (Maya).

Appendix: simple math example
- Tenant reserved_units = 4 normalized-vGPU units; shaping_window = 60s -> steady tokens = 4 * 60 = 240 normalized-vGPU-sec per minute.
- max_burst_ratio = 3 -> allowed tokens in short window = 720 normalized-vGPU-sec; burst fabric can satisfy extra 480 if available.
- If burst_pool_total = 5000 normalized-vGPU-sec and current_utilization=60%, automated top-ups will attempt to grant up to tenant max for short windows.

End of notes.

(This file is intentionally a mix of PRD bullets + engineering notes; intended to be iterated into a polished PRD.)
